subject: Engagement roadmap: eval access, org setup, IP allowlist & VPC peering
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@medsyst.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@medsyst.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Engagement roadmap: eval access, org setup, IP allowlist & VPC peering

Hi Claire / Samir —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation, I pulled together a short engagement roadmap to get your evaluation environment live and to target a clean close within the 4–6 week window we discussed. Below are the minimal items we need on your side, plus recommended owners and target dates so you can slot these into your procurement/IT cadence.

High-level goal: org invite + API keys and network access provisioned so MedSyst engineers can run the evaluation workload (hipaa-simulated data) by 2027-05-20.

Action items (owner — target):
- MedSyst org invite to Redwood (Claire) — 2027-05-12: invite via admin console; role: Org Admin + Billing (temp).
- Short-lived API key creation (Redwood) — Evelyn/Marissa: create scoped API key (30-day eval) and share secure link — 2027-05-13.
- IP allowlist (MedSyst) — Samir: provide CIDR(s) for egress/static NAT that should be permitted — 2027-05-13. We prefer a small set / single CIDR for simplicity.
- VPC peering (optional, higher isolation) — Samir / MedSyst Networking: provide VPC name/ID, AWS account ID, and preferred CIDR to peer — target kickoff 2027-05-14; peer complete by 2027-05-18 if you choose this path.
- Procurement/PO (MedSyst purchasing) — Claire: confirm PO window / any required contract language (SOC 2, DPA references) — target 2027-05-17.
- Security questionnaire & evidence (MedSyst security) — Marissa: we will send SOC2 summary and data retention doc; please flag any additional evidence required — 2027-05-14.

Notes / clarifications:
- API keys: For the eval we will issue a scoped key limited to the test models and a 30-day expiration. Keys are revocable and logged in the Console. If you prefer service-account-based tokens (for automation), note that we support signed service tokens — call these out in your reply.
- Allowlist vs. peering: allowlisting static CIDR is the fastest path (minutes after you provide ranges). VPC peering provides stronger network isolation but requires your infra team to open a peering request and accept routes; plan ~3 business days.
- Data handling: Redwood does not store customer data beyond retention windows you choose for the eval; we will provide the data handling section in the attachments.

Attached: draft engagement plan (map), network allowlist template, and a DocuSign acknowledgement we can use to capture mutual acceptance of the timeline.

Next step: can you confirm who will be the point for networking and procurement so we can assign owners and lock dates?

Thanks —
Evelyn

--
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: medsyst-map-draft.pdf (32 KB)]
[Attachment: network-allowlist-template.csv (1 KB)]
[Attachment: docusign-map-acknowledgement-link.txt (link)]

From: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@medsyst.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@medsyst.com>
Date: 2027-05-11T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Engagement roadmap: eval access, org setup, IP allowlist & VPC peering

Evelyn — thanks for the clear plan. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) Procurement: we will need a PO in place before we spin up anything persistent. Short-lived eval keys should be fine while legal finalizes the PO — we typically allow sandbox access under a non-production clause.
2) Networking: our infra team prefers VPC peering for anything that touches PHI-like datasets; static egress addresses are OK but we'd need NAT Gateway IPs (we can provide them).
3) Security: SOC 2 summary should be shared — can you include any pen-test summary or attestations? Our security team will also ask for logging details and retention period.

People:
- Networking: Samir Patel (samir.patel@medsyst.com)
- Purchasing: Claire Thompson (procurement)
- Security reviewer: Karen Liu (karen.liu@medsyst.com) — she may ping you for a short questionnaire.

If you can send the short-lived key and the DocuSign acknowledgement link today, we can get the PO started and schedule peering work for early next week.

Claire

- Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-11T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Engagement roadmap: eval access, org setup, IP allowlist & VPC peering

Hi all —

Thanks Claire — quick notes from infra side:
- If you prefer peering, we need: AWS account ID (12 digits), VPC ID, and the CIDR range you expect to use. We will initiate the peering from our side once you accept. Expect 48–72 hours to complete with route table updates.
- If you want to start immediately, paste your NAT public IPs into the attached CSV and we will apply allowlist entries within one business hour after verification.
- Ports required for the eval: 443 outbound to Redwood endpoints; no inbound ports are required.

Attachments I just shared: network-allowlist-template.csv (please fill column A with the public IP / CIDR), and a peering checklist doc. I also included a short TekOps note on verifying TLS fingerprints if you want to pin them.

We will: create a scoped API key (Evelyn / Marissa will post the secure link), and also upload SOC2 summary to the shared link for Karen to review.

Rishi
